title: Smart surgical instruments and systems with integrated sensor telemetry
abstract: A surgical instrument system includes an end effector, an articulation joint, a drive assembly, and an electronic control system. The control system continuously monitors telemetry from sensors on the end effector to dynamically regulate tissue clamping pressure and motor current.
claims: Claim 1: A surgical instrument comprising: an end effector configured to grasp tissue; a sensor array positioned on the end effector to measure real-time tissue impedance; and a microcontroller configured to modulate motor drive current based on said impedance.
Claim 2: The surgical instrument of claim 1, further comprising an articulation joint coupled to the end effector and an electromechanical actuator responsive to the microcontroller.
description:
Background of the Invention
Surgical stapling and cutting devices require precise force management to prevent tissue damage while ensuring secure staple formation. Traditional mechanical linkages lack real-time feedback under variable tissue thickness.

Summary of the Invention
The present invention provides an integrated sensor feedback loop that continuously samples tissue characteristics and dynamically throttles actuator displacement.

title: Generating contextual summaries from multi-source electronic documents
abstract: Methods and systems for generating contextual summaries from electronic documents using entity graph extraction and cross-reference frequency weighting. Candidate summary sentences are scored based on semantic centrality and topical cohesion.
claims: Claim 1: A method for generating contextual summaries comprising: parsing a plurality of input documents to identify named entities; constructing an entity-relation co-occurrence graph; and ranking sentences according to eigenvector centrality on said graph.
Claim 2: The method of claim 1, further comprising filtering redundant sentences whose cosine similarity exceeds a predefined threshold.
description:
Background
Large text corpora present significant challenge for knowledge workers attempting to distill key insights across disparate technical specifications.

Detailed Description
The system creates an entity-centric summary by linking concepts across documents and extracting representative sentence clusters.

title: Document chunking and hierarchical indexing for dense semantic retrieval
abstract: Hierarchical segmentation and semantic chunking of semi-structured documents for vector similarity search. Text passages are chunked along structural headings and syntactic sentence boundaries to preserve local semantic context.
claims: Claim 1: A computer-implemented system comprising: a structural parser configured to identify heading levels in a document; a chunking engine configured to segment content between heading levels into bounded passages with rolling overlap; and an embedding index storing vector representations of each passage.
Claim 2: The system of claim 1, wherein the bounded passages enforce strict sentence boundary alignment.
description:
Technical Field
The present disclosure relates generally to information retrieval and document indexing for dense neural representations.

Detailed Description
Document passages are divided into contiguous chunks that preserve heading context as structural metadata alongside passage text.

title: Information retrieval using hybrid lexical and dense vector representations
abstract: Systems and methods for ranking search candidates using reciprocal rank fusion over sparse lexical inverted indices and dense embedding projections. Combined scoring balances keyword exact matches with semantic intent.
claims: Claim 1: A search system comprising: a lexical retrieval engine producing a first ranked list of document identifiers; a dense vector retrieval engine producing a second ranked list of document identifiers; and a rank fusion engine combining said first and second ranked lists via reciprocal rank fusion.
Claim 2: The search system of claim 1, wherein reciprocal rank fusion assigns scores according to the formula 1/(k + rank).
description:
Background
Purely lexical search engines miss synonymy and paraphrasing, whereas dense vector models can fail on rare technical alphanumeric codes.

title: Automated claim-to-prior-art mapping and novelty evaluation system
abstract: Natural language processing methods for decomposing patent claims into technical limitations and mapping each limitation against prior art reference passages to evaluate novelty and obviousness.
claims: Claim 1: An apparatus for patent claim evaluation comprising: a parser configured to decompose an independent patent claim into individual technical limitations; a retriever configured to query a prior-art corpus for candidate passages corresponding to each limitation; and a scoring engine that computes an evidence coverage score.
Claim 2: The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the evidence coverage score represents the proportion of limitations corroborated by at least one prior art passage.
description:
Field of the Invention
The present invention relates to intellectual property analytics, particularly computerized systems for evaluating patent novelty against existing prior art disclosures.

title: Graph-based knowledge representation and multi-hop reasoning over technical literature
abstract: Constructing multi-relational knowledge graphs from technical patent corpora and performing graph neural network inference to detect conceptual overlap and latent prior art connections across disparate domains.
claims: Claim 1: A system comprising: one or more processors configured to extract entity nodes and relation edges from technical patent publications; populate a heterogeneous knowledge graph; and execute multi-hop path traversal to link disparate technical claims.
Claim 2: The system of claim 1, wherein entity nodes comprise chemical compounds, mechanical components, and algorithmic processes.
description:
Background
Prior-art documents often express identical underlying technical principles using divergent terminology across different industrial sectors.

title: Neural re-ranking and cross-encoder scoring for document retrieval
abstract: A two-stage information retrieval architecture wherein initial candidates from lexical and embedding retrieval are scored using a cross-attention transformer that jointly processes query and passage tokens.
claims: Claim 1: A method of re-ranking document passages comprising: receiving a set of top-k document candidates from a bi-encoder retrieval index; forming paired query-passage token sequences; and passing each paired sequence through a cross-encoder transformer to compute a relevance probability.
Claim 2: The method of claim 1, wherein the top-k document candidates are selected via approximate nearest neighbor search.
description:
Detailed Description
Cross-encoder architectures evaluate all-to-all cross attention between query terms and candidate document passages, resolving contextual ambiguity.

title: Patent classification and prior art identification using deep convolutional networks
abstract: Multi-label classification of patent disclosures across IPC and CPC hierarchies using character-level and word-level neural representations. Class predictions guide selective prior-art partition filtering.
claims: Claim 1: A method for hierarchical patent categorization comprising: encoding an abstract and independent claims into dense representation vectors; classifying said vectors into one or more CPC subclasses; and routing retrieval queries to corresponding index shards.
Claim 2: The method of claim 1, wherein the classification model outputs calibrated confidence probabilities for each predicted subclass.
description:
Background of the Invention
Patent databases contain millions of filings organized into fine-grained classification taxonomies requiring automated categorization.

title: Contradiction detection and evidence verification in technical patent specifications
abstract: Verifying technical assertions against empirical evidence extracted from scientific literature and patent databases using natural language inference and contradiction scoring.
claims: Claim 1: A computer system configured to: extract factual claim premises from a technical document; search an evidence repository for topical evidence passages; and calculate an entailment score, neutral score, and contradiction score for each premise.
Claim 2: The system of claim 1, wherein an overall verification report highlights premises exhibiting contradiction scores above a predetermined threshold.
description:
Summary of the Invention
Technical and patent claims are automatically verified against external literature repositories to detect false assertions or prior-art conflicts.

title: Multi-vector document retrieval with reciprocal rank fusion
abstract: A retrieval engine that executes separate sparse lexical and dense semantic queries, fusing ranked list outputs via reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) with position-weighted decay constants.
claims: Claim 1: A method comprising: performing a BM25 lexical search for a user query against a text index; performing a cosine similarity vector search for an embedding of said query against a vector index; and computing fused scores for candidate documents using reciprocal rank fusion.
Claim 2: The method of claim 1, wherein reciprocal rank fusion applies a tuning parameter k where k is between 20 and 100.
description:
Background
Search engines combining BM25 keyword matching and dense vector search provide higher recall than either technique in isolation.

title: Semantic indexing and concept retrieval for intellectual property assets
abstract: Ontology-driven concept indexing for patent claims and specifications enabling semantic search across patent families and foreign language equivalents.
assignee: LexisNexis, a division of RELX Inc.
claims: Claim 1: A method for semantic patent indexing comprising: mapping text in patent claims to standardized ontology concept nodes; linking parent-child relationships between concepts; and indexing patent documents by said ontology concepts.
Claim 2: The method of claim 1, further comprising mapping foreign language terms into corresponding canonical ontology concepts.
description:
Detailed Description
Patents across international jurisdictions are normalized against a unified domain ontology to enable cross-border prior art search.

title: Automated extraction of technical limitations from patent claim language
abstract: Decomposing preamble, transitional phrase, and body elements of patent claims into structured limitation tuples to evaluate claim breadth and scope.
claims: Claim 1: A system comprising: a natural language parser that segments a patent claim into preamble, transitional phrase, and limitation clauses; and a limitation extractor that structures each limitation into an action, object, and condition tuple.
Claim 2: The system of claim 1, wherein the transitional phrase is classified as open-ended comprising or closed-ended consisting of.
description:
Background
Determining the scope of patent protection requires breaking claims down into distinct limitations to check for literal infringement or anticipation.

title: Zero-shot technical entity linking across multi-lingual patent disclosures
abstract: Cross-lingual entity linking and semantic disambiguation across Japanese, Chinese, and English patent corpora using bilingual bi-encoders.
claims: Claim 1: A method for multilingual entity linking in patents: embedding technical entities from a first language document; mapping said entities into a shared multilingual embedding space; and identifying equivalent concepts in a second language document.
Claim 2: The method of claim 1, wherein the multilingual embedding space is trained using aligned patent abstracts.
description:
Technical Field
The invention enables global patent searchers to discover prior art filed in foreign patent offices without manual translation.

title: Dynamic prior art clustering and citation landscape visualization
abstract: Real-time clustering and topographic mapping of forward and backward patent citations to reveal prior-art crowding and white spaces for invention planning.
claims: Claim 1: A computer system comprising: a citation graph builder that constructs directional citation links between patent publications; a dimensional reduction engine that projects patents onto a 2D topographical manifold; and a visualization UI displaying clusters and unoccupied white spaces.
Claim 2: The computer system of claim 1, wherein cluster boundaries are colored according to patent filing velocity.
description:
Background of the Invention
R&D teams need to understand the density of competitive patent filings to steer new product development away from crowded prior art.

title: Multi-stage patent readiness and patentability assessment using evidence weighting
abstract: Evaluating patent readiness of technical invention drafts by computing feature-level overlap ratios, novelty indices, and evidence-grounded similarity scores against prior-art corpus passages.
claims: Claim 1: A method for assessing patent readiness: receiving an invention draft; extracting a set of technical features; retrieving candidate prior art documents; computing feature-level semantic overlap scores; and generating an evidence-based patent readiness score.
Claim 2: The method of claim 1, wherein features are weighted according to novelty criticality and technical feasibility.
description:
Detailed Description
The system computes a multi-dimensional readiness evaluation combining novelty, technical depth, and prior-art risk indices.
